newsitem.title: ITALY: Denmark will take part in Albania mission - minister.
newsitem.headline: Denmark will take part in Albania mission - minister.

text.p: Denmark will send troops to join a multinational security mission in Albania, Danish Foreign Minister Niels Helveg Petersen said on Monday.

The operation, which has been sanctioned by the United Nations to protect the distribution of food and medical aid in the anarchic Balkan state, is being orchestrated by Italy and is due to swing into action this week.

"Denmark will take part in the Italian-led force in Albania. The Danish parliament later this week will be presented with a proposal," Petersen told a news conference after meeting his Italian counterpart, Lamberto Dini.
He declined to say how many troops Denmark intended to send, but Dini said the number was not important.
"The important thing is that Denmark will participate. The size of the contingent is irrelevant in respect to the participation," Dini told reporters.
Denmark is the seventh country to pledge soldiers to the mission after Italy, France, Greece, Spain, Turkey and Romania. Austria is also considering participation.
So far some 6,000 troops have been commited, with Italy alone providing 2,500 men.
The main bulk of the Italian contingent is due to start deploying in Albania from Tuesday. Forward parties from Italy and France are already in Albania to prepare for the operation.
